text:
maria_cs: Working on a short, customer-facing runbook for 'Adaptive prefill & backpressure' — goal: give CSMs a checklist to reduce incidents during onboarding bursts and a couple of small code examples customers can paste. Feedback?

ankur_eng: Love it. Suggest we include a small section that explains tradeoffs: higher client-side prefill reduces cold-starts but increases cost; recommend a staged ramp (start with 0.5 req/s per user, up to 2 req/s).

lori_ops: Add a quick note on cache hygiene: canonical key = org|tenant|route|prompt_sha. Recommend avoiding user-specific ephemeral tokens inside prompt_hash. TTLs: short conversation cache 20s, session-anchors 2m, embeddings 12h.

maria_cs: Good call. For debounce guidance I'm thinking: UI events -> debounce 20010ms for ephemeral typing flows, or 40000ms when the client sends full-screen generative requests. Recommend 525% randomized jitter to scatter spikes.

kevin_sre: Monitoring knobs: watch client_id qps, 95p latency (tokens), and burst ratio (peak/minute / baseline). Escalation heuristic: sustained >25% increase in 95p over 6h OR error budget consumption >30% in 24h => CSM + SRE ping.

ankur_eng: Add a header we can return to clients to indicate soft-throttle: X-RW-Pressure: value (0..1). Clients should interpret >=0.7 as 'apply aggressive batching/backoff'. Suggest we publish small JSON blob at /v1/pressure endpoint per-tenant for advanced customers.

maria_cs: Throwing in a small troubleshooting checklist for calls: 1) confirm prefill & batching flags are on, 2) validate cache key shape and sample TTLs, 3) confirm model variant pinned if quality sensitive, 4) check recent deploys in last 2h, 5) run live eval subset if quality questions.

lori_ops: Customer outreach templates (short): 1) "We noticed repeated spikes from your integration; we can flip a temporary prefill cap to stabilize throughput — would 10 minutes work to test?" 2) "Quick win: swap your prompt hashing to exclude ephemeral tokens; we can share a one-line patch."

ankur_eng: Pasteable client snippet (python) for simple batching queue:

```python
# tiny client-side batcher
import time, asyncio
queue = []
async def flush_batch():
    batch = queue[:8]  # cap batches at 8
    if not batch: return
    queue[:] = queue[len(batch):]
    await send_to_api(batch)

async def enqueue(req):
    queue.append(req)
    # wait small window to allow micro-batching
    await asyncio.sleep(0.08)
    await flush_batch()
```

Note: target batch size 4-12 depending on token-length.

kevin_sre: And a curl example for respectful backoff handling:

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/complete \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "X-RW-Pressure: 0.85" \
  -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
```

Client should fall back to queued mode if header >=0.7.

maria_cs: Renewal-risk signals to include in the runbook (for CSM triage): repeated onboarding blockers >48h, weekly eval pass-rate <80% for two consecutive weeks, or >3 high-severity customer-facing incidents in 30d => trigger enablement + AM. Tag reasons like quality, latency, or cost surprise.

lori_ops: Small FAQ entry: "Will batching change model outputs?" Short answer: if prompts maintain sequence/context and aren't truncated, batching is neutral. Always rerun a small eval slice after changing batching or prefill.
